Header: Bidens pilosa Sere (Luganda), Laabika (Acholi), Ononot (Langi), Kalaala (Lusoga)

Prevention: Purchase and sow certified seeds from recognised agro input dealer.
Where home saved seed is to be used ensure it is free of blackjack seeds
Do not allow livestock into a blackjack infested areas because they spread the seed
For humans ensure that you are not carrying any weed seed on your body, shoes and clothing.
In case you are carrying any seed, remove and destroy by burning
Avoid run off through the fields by making soil bunds because seeds are easily spread by water from surrounding infested fields
Slash or mow the weed in land within the vicinity before it flowers to avoid spread by wind
Maize varieties that can support high population densities can suppress weed infestation for example
Monitoring: Annual erect broadleaved weed (up to 1m high) with green composed leaves and a strong taproot.
Flowers white with yellow centre and 1cm long black seeds with 2-4 yellowish awns at one end
Regularly check surroundings for presence of weed every 3-4 weeks, or any time you can access the surroundings
Regulary check fields for weed infestation.
Removal) of 1-2 and 2-3 weeks under heavy and low infestation respectively
Check for flowering and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank
Direct Control: Dig up or hand pull plants prior to onset of flowering, ensuring the taproot is severed well below the crown (2-5 inches) to prevent regrowth
A maize-bean intercropping system can effectively suppress the weed
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Diuron (500g per litre of active ingredient per hectare), Atrazine, Hexazinone (2.5 to 10kg per litre of active ingredient per hectare), and
Ametryn (2 to 4kg per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
D (720g per litre of active ingredient per hectare), metribuzin (0.6 to 1 kg per litre of active ingredient per acre)
and dicamba (500g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
Contact herbicides: bentazone (480g per litre of active ingredient per hectare)
